subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Allen Stanford's Fake Bank
description: A quick, practical guide to Allen Stanford's Fake Bank.

hook.text: Allen Stanford sold $7 billion in fake certificates of deposit from a bank in Antigua.

buildup.text: His bank offered consistently high returns. Investors believed his claims of a secret investment strategy.

discovery.text: The money was used to fund Stanford's lifestyle — private jets, cricket tournaments, and real estate.

twist.text: Antiguan regulators were in on it, receiving payments to look the other way for years.

climax.text: Stanford was sentenced to 110 years in prison — one of the harshest white-collar sentences ever.

punchline.text: The bank was in Antigua. The fraud was all-American.

quiz.question: How long was Allen Stanford's prison sentence?
